newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-ALLEN JOHNSON PRODUCES BEST WHEN IT MATTERS MOST.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-ALLEN JOHNSON PRODUCES BEST WHEN IT MATTERS MOST.

text.p: Allen Johnson, spurred by the presence of world record holder Colin Jackson, produced his best when it mattered most on Thursday to retain his world high hurdles title.

The American Olympic champion brushed five barriers but still held off Jackson in a time of 12.93 seconds, just two-hundredths of a second outside the mark set by Jackson at the 1993 Stuttgart world championships.
"That was tough," Johnson said. "I got to the first hurdle first because I knew Colin would get a great start."
Jackson added: "I think that Allen and I will both get under 12.90 this season. Allen was fantastic."

The sixth day of the sixth world championships began with Pole Robert Korzeniowski, an avowed fan of cool weather, winning the 50 kms walk in fierce morning heat plus the first drugs scandal of the championships.

Ukrainian shot putter Alexandr Bagach, who won the first gold medal of the championships last Saturday, was stripped of his gold medal and lost $60,000 prize money after testing positive for the stimulant ephedrine.
French 400 metres hurdler Pascal Maran and women's triple jumper Oxana Zelinskaya of Kazakhstan also had their results annulled after positive tests for the same drug.
Since the relaxation of the International Amateur Athletic Federation's drugs rules, the trio will receive a "public warning" only although Bagach has been previously banned for doping.
Bagach maintained his innocence on Thursday afternoon.
"Basically I used this supplement which is made of natural substances and does not mention that it has ephedrine in it," Bagach told Reuters Television.

In the field events, Astrid Kumbernuss of Germany retained her world shot put title and New Zealand's Beatrice Faumuina won her country's first medal of any kind at the 14-year-old championships with victory in the women's discus.
Italian Annarita Sidoti won the women's 10 kms walk, profiting from the disqualification of defending champion Irina Stankina of Russia.
Marie Jose-Perec's world championship hopes ended in tears when she pulled a leg muscle while warming up for the 200 metres semifinals.
The double Olympic champion, who had not planned to compete here, said: "I guess it just wasn't my year. The years after the Olympics are always the tough ones for me."
